Nitriles (compounds containing the -C≡N functional group) can react with acids, especially strong acids, to produce hydrogen cyanide (HCN) gas. Hydrogen cyanide is highly toxic and can be fatal if inhaled. This is one of the primary hazards when mixing nitriles with organic acids.

The reaction involves the protonation of the nitrile nitrogen by the acid, which can lead to the formation of toxic hydrogen cyanide gas. This is particularly concerning in acidic conditions or when heated.
